title: American roast turkey
subtitle: Classic Thanksgiving roast turkey with herb butter under the skin
excerpt: A whole turkey rubbed under and over the skin with herb butter, roasted low and slow, and rested for a full 30 minutes. Served with pan drippings gravy. The Thanksgiving centrepiece, done properly.
sourceNotes: Roast turkey has been the centrepiece of American Thanksgiving since the mid-nineteenth century, following Sarah Josepha Hale's 1863 campaign to make Thanksgiving a national holiday. The herb-butter-under-skin technique appears in modern American roasting references. Fannie Farmer's The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896, public domain) includes detailed turkey roasting instructions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The herb butter can be made and applied 2 days ahead. Keep refrigerated and bring to room temperature before roasting.
recipe.temperatureNote: after initial 220°C blast to colour the skin

content.text: Roasting a whole turkey well requires two things: getting the herb butter under the skin to baste the breast meat from inside, and resting the bird for long enough that the juices redistribute. An instant-read thermometer is not optional. The breast is done at 71°C and the thigh at 74°C; without a thermometer you are guessing.

items.prepNote: 5 kg turkey, room temperature; giblets removed
sprigs, leaves stripped and finely chopped

content.text: Mix the butter with the garlic, herbs, lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Starting from the neck end of the turkey, use your fingers to loosen the skin from the breast meat, creating a pocket. Push two-thirds of the herb butter under the skin and spread it as evenly as possible over the breast. Rub the remaining butter all over the outside of the bird. Season the cavity with salt.
Stuff the cavity loosely with the onion and lemon halves. Tie the legs together with kitchen string. Pour the stock into the bottom of the roasting tin. Heat the oven to 220°C (fan 200°C).

Roast at 220°C for 20 minutes to colour the skin. Reduce the heat to 180°C (fan 160°C). Continue roasting, basting every 45 minutes with the pan juices. For a 5 kg bird: approximately 3.5 to 4 hours total. Check the internal temperature: the breast should read 71°C and the thickest part of the thigh (not touching bone) should read 74°C.

Transfer the turkey to a board and cover loosely with foil and a couple of tea towels. Rest for 45 minutes minimum. The temperature will rise 2 to 3°C during resting. Use the pan drippings to make gravy.

items.cause: Over-roasted; breast reached too high a temperature
items.fix: Use a thermometer to pull the bird at exactly 71°C in the breast. The rest is essential: a minimum of 30 minutes, 45 is better.

items.symptom: Skin is pale and not crisp
items.cause: Too much steam in the oven, or skin was wet when roasting started
items.fix: Pat the skin completely dry before adding the butter. Don't cover the tin with foil.

content.text: Roast turkey is the Thanksgiving centrepiece. The American family meal has been organised around it since 1863, when Abraham Lincoln declared the national holiday at Sarah Josepha Hale's instigation. Turkey was already part of the New World food supply by the seventeenth century. English settlers brought the whole-bird roast. It became thoroughly Americanised over time. Today it is inseparable from cranberry sauce, stuffing, and sweet potato casserole.
